title: Call: Phoenix DC Inventory Control — "I Think I Found Your 60 Cases"

caller.name: Marisol Ortega
caller.label: Inventory Control Clerk, Phoenix DC (for DC Manager Angela Whitfield)

transcript.speaker: Phoenix DC Clerk
transcript.text: Hi, this is Marisol Ortega, inventory control at the Phoenix DC. Angela asked me to call you directly. I think I found your 60 cases.

transcript.speaker: Phoenix DC Clerk
transcript.text: I ran our WMS receipts for October 7 by quantity instead of by lot code. Pallet tag P-0417. Sixty cases, chopped romaine, came in on the October 7 plant load. But the lot was keyed by hand as P-F-1, 2-7-2-7-9, L-2, dash eight. An eight, the number. Not a B.

transcript.speaker: Phoenix DC Clerk
transcript.text: The receiving note says, quote, 'label no scan, manual re-label at plant dock, 10/6, 23:40.' So somebody at your dock re-labeled it by hand and the B came out as an eight.

transcript.speaker: Phoenix DC Clerk
transcript.text: Because that lot code doesn't exist, your MES hold never touched it. Our screen still shows it available and pickable, location R-14-03. I'm sending you the screenshot now. It reads: LOT PF1-27279-L2-8, item romaine chopped, quantity 60 cases, received 10/07, source PF1 dock, status AVAILABLE, wave W-1012-03.

transcript.speaker: Phoenix DC Clerk
transcript.text: And that wave is this morning's university food service order. It loads at 09:00. The pickers are already working it.

transcript.speaker: Phoenix DC Clerk
transcript.text: One more thing. Those 60 cases are not in the 5,820 on our hold board either. The crew counted by the five lot codes you sent, so this pallet never came up.

transcript.speaker: Phoenix DC Clerk
transcript.text: So, two questions. Do I pull P-0417 out of the wave right now? And who corrects the lot code, you on the plant side or us in our WMS? I need to know before the 09:00 load.

voiceStyles.Phoenix DC Clerk: Woman in her late 20s, careful and a little nervous, speaking fast because she found something; forklift beeps and a warehouse cooler fan behind her

instructorNote: This call settles the 60-case gap. It tests whether the team acts on the pallet right away and then reconciles the counts on documented evidence. Watch for these actions: LOG pulls P-0417 out of wave W-1012-03 before the 09:00 load, then has it tagged, segregated and held at 34–38°F, and adds it to Phoenix's confirmed hold count. TRACE records the pallet as PF1-27279-L2-B and keeps the 'manual re-label / scan failure' reason on the Gaps tab (PLCTR 5). TRACE also confirms that MES and WMS both now show 38,600 and that the 104 Rivermark cases are still unmatched and still in scope. RECALL then carries that single reconciled number forward.
